title: The Transitions panel stays out of the way: closed until there is a cut to work on, and still until you hover a tile
goal: Opening a video shows the inspector's Transitions section already open with nothing picked, and every transition tile in it animates nonstop. It is noise: it pulls the eye away from the video, does nothing useful with nothing picked, and costs CPU. The section should only be open when there is a cut to work on, and its tiles should be still pictures that play their motion only while the pointer is over one.
notes: User, 2026-10-30 (intake): 'i opened a video editor and the transitions panel is both 1. open (it doesn't even need to be there when i have nothing selected) and 2. animating every possible transition obnoxiously'. Code: the section is InspectorSection .transitions (InspectorSections.swift ~218, InspectorPanel.swift ~2102 shows TransitionsGroup()). Each tile in TransitionsGroup.swift tile(_:) renders VideoKit.AnimatedTransitionThumbnail, which animates all the time; the same view is used in TransitionPicker.swift and LibraryCatalogTiles.swift. The picker-at-the-cut task (500f1363, choosing-a-transition-between-two-clips-is-one-o) asked for 'A tile plays its motion on hover', not always. Related: the CPU complaint 2026-10-28 where WindowServer sat at 45 to 55% while things on screen redrew constantly.
acceptance: At Next defaults, opening a recording (and a new video) with nothing picked: the Transitions section is collapsed or not shown at all. It opens on its own when a cut is picked or clicked, and goes back to how the person left it after. A person who opens it by hand and leaves it open is respected across launches.

Transition tiles everywhere (the inspector's Transitions section, the picker at a cut, the Library catalog) are still at rest, showing a representative frame of their motion. A tile plays its motion only while the pointer is over it, and stops when the pointer leaves. Nothing animates on screen unless the person is hovering it or playing the video.

Measured, in the audit: WindowServer and app CPU with the video editor open and idle, before and after (today every tile runs its own animation). After: no frame is drawn by the panel while idle, checked with a frame counter or Instruments.

Walks: open a recording with nothing picked and the section is not open; pick a cut and it opens; hover a tile and it moves; leave and it stops. Screenshots before and after in the audit under queue/audits/.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: triage 2026-10-30: the picker at a cut already rests still and plays on hover since 500f1363 (choosing-a-transition-between-two-clips-is-one-o), but that task changed only the picker; the inspector's Transitions section and the Library catalog still use the always-playing tile. Make the three share one tile so they cannot drift again.

triage 2026-10-30, left rough (not added to acceptance, the user's call): ten of the twelve tiles carry the fixed note 'needs overlap' (ClipTransitionKind.note, from the mock's video-transition-wt.html tiles), shown even on a cut with spare footage (audit picture 2026-10-29-transition-at-the-cut-3-tiles-at-the-cut.png: spare 1.1s / 1.9s and every tile says needs overlap). Since 2026-10-29 every one of them goes on any cut, holding frames where footage runs out, so the note now reads like a refusal the app no longer makes. Raised in the 2026-10-30 digest for the user to decide, since it is the mock's own copy.

Adversarial pass: a Premiere user finds Video Transitions in the Effects panel collapsed by default and opens it when they want one; folding it until a cut is picked matches that, and holding it open while a cut is in hand puts the tiles where the click will land. Risk: someone who opened it by hand expects it to stay; covered, a hand open is stored (+transitions) and survives launches.

Chose a hold (open while a cut is picked, never stored) over writing the fold, because the acceptance says it goes back to how the person left it. A header click while held folds it and it stays folded; commands that open a section store it open.

Chose one shared tile (TransitionTileFace, TransitionPicker.swift) for the picker, the panel and the Library, resting on restingProgress and playing a TimelineView lap from its start on hover; removed VideoKit.AnimatedTransitionThumbnail and ProgressLoop, which nothing else used.

Measured: paired captures 0.5s apart, before 27,876 / 119,627 changed pixels idle (nothing picked / cut picked), after 0 / 0; hover 14,003, left 0. App CPU unchanged (Core Animation played the old reels), WindowServer at 61% with no Photonz running, so not attributable. Pictures looked at: before nothing picked (open, tiles), after nothing picked (folded), cut picked (open, still), hover, let go (folded).

Walks: every-section-header-opens, section-fold-motion and transitions-group updated for Transitions starting folded; all three fail at the same steps they failed in this morning's sweep on old code (header presses and a drop not landing), owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26. New walk transitions-stay-out-of-the-way-walk passes at defaults.

Transitions starts folded, is held open while a cut is picked and folds back after; a hand open is stored. One shared still-until-hovered tile in the picker, the panel and the Library. Verified: 14,802 tests green, new transitions-stay-out-of-the-way-walk passes at defaults, idle captures 0 changed pixels (27,876 / 119,627 before).
